LESSON: INTRODUCTION TO DRAWING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.1: Introduction to Drawing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Introduction to Drawing, part of Communication in Pre-Technical Studies in Grade 7 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are drawings used in technical communication?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the importance of drawing as a means of communication,

2. brainstorm on the meaning of the terms ‘technical drawing’ and ‘artistic drawing,

3. use print or online resources to search for information on artistic and technical drawing,

4. practice printing numbers and letters of the alphabet,

5. use visual aids to search for information on the types of lines and their application in drawing (thick and thin continuous, dashed, and chain).

6. draw various types of lines (thick and thin continuous, dashed and chain)

7. sketch basic symbols (⌀, ℄, R, ⊥, ▢) and abbreviations

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the importance of drawing as a means of communication,
2. brainstorm on the meaning of the terms ‘technical drawing’ and ‘artistic drawing,
3. use print or online resources to search for information on artistic and technical drawing,
4. practice printing numbers and letters of the alphabet,
5. use visual aids to search for information on the types of lines and their application in drawing (thick and thin continuous, dashed, and chain).
6. draw various types of lines (thick and thin continuous, dashed and chain)
7. sketch basic symbols (⌀, ℄, R, ⊥, ▢) and abbreviations

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Introduction to Drawing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: the learner acquires speaking, listening and teamwork skills when brainstorming on the

meaning of the terms ‘technical drawing’ and ‘artistic drawing’.

• Digital Literacy: learner develops the skill of interacting with technology when using online resources to search for

information on artistic and technical drawing.

Values:
• Respect: learner demonstrates etiquette during discussion of basic symbols and abbreviations used in drawing.

• Responsibility: learner demonstrates accountability when using visual aids to search for information on the types of lines and

their application in drawing.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and Security: the learner develops online safety skills during online search for information on different types of drawings

used in the technical fields.

Link to other Subjects:

Creative Arts: learner enhances knowledge of artistic drawing when drawing various types of lines in Pre-Technical studies.
